title: Require a specific, accurate adverse-action explanation whenever an automated system contributes to a credit decision
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on the Apple Card/Goldman Sachs gender-bias allegations and the resulting NYDFS investigation. Not a documented decision of any specific organisation.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

decision_statement: Whenever an automated or algorithmic system contributes to a credit, lending, or pricing decision, the organisation must be able to give the affected individual a specific, accurate reason for any adverse outcome — model complexity is not an acceptable excuse for a vague or generic explanation.
decision_context: Motivated by the Apple Card/Goldman Sachs credit-limit controversy, in which public allegations of gender bias could not be quickly confirmed or refuted because neither the company nor the applicants could point to a specific, individualised explanation of the underwriting decision.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Algorithmic Underwriting Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Provide only a generic adverse-action notice citing 'creditworthiness' without individualised reasons.
Treat model complexity as a valid reason to withhold a specific explanation.

citations.title: Report on Apple Card Investigation
citations.publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services

relationships.reason: This decision is modelled as a direct governance response to this incident.
The decision is put into practice via this design pattern.
A specific adverse-action reason directly satisfies this control's notice requirement.
Compliance must be demonstrated by a documented adverse-action notice record.
Boards adopting this decision should be asking whether specific reasons can actually be produced on demand.
